title: Route IO-mode latency snapshotboard and trace-linked anomaly swimlane
creator: Ravi Shah
description: Build a dedicated snapshotboard that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency by model + route with an explicit split between streaming and non-streaming (blocking) requests, and a companion trace-linked anomaly swimlane that quickly maps sudden percentile regressions to traces, KV-cache hit patterns, and recent rollout changes.
context: Existing latency surfaces are fragmented: multiple trendboards show percentiles but lack a compact cross-cut that highlights IO-mode deltas (stream chunking vs blocking token bursts), and trace links are inconsistent for streaming requests. This makes incident TTR longer when model/route regressions are IO-mode specific.
goals: Single-pane snapshotboard for ops showing p50/p95/p99 by (model, route) with streaming vs blocking columns
Trace-linked anomaly swimlane that pins a percentile spike to specific traces and KV-cache / prefix-hit signals
Low-latency alerting hooks for >2x p95 delta on streaming vs blocking for high-traffic routes
Instrument trace hooks and log/metric schema changes with minimal cardinality cost (sampling plan included)
success_metrics: Reduce average time-to-root-cause for route IO-mode regressions from 42m to <15m
Alert precision: <25% false positives on streaming-vs-blocking delta alerts after 2-week tuning
Dashboard adoption: ops/SECs add snapshotboard to daily watchlist within 2 weeks of release
scope: Dashboard panels + queries, trace hook upgrades for streaming requests, metrics/log pipeline schema additions, alert rules, and runbook updates.
out_of_scope: Re-architecting serving runtime (kernel selection) or adding new model variants. Model rollout automation is separate (see Dedicated rollout epic).
infra_changes: Introduce histogram buckets aligned with token-generation latency (25ms, 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2s, 5s)
Emit streamChunkLatency span for streaming flows and correlating attribute 'chunk_index' and 'request_shape'
Add kv_cache_hit boolean tag and prefix_hit_ratio metric emitted at request completion
Update logging schema: trace_id, route, model_version, io.mode, request_size_bytes, tokens_generated
queries_snippets: Panel: p50/p95/p99 heatmap by model,route,io.mode -> metrics query using request_latency.histogram filtered by io.mode
Swimlane: group by route and 5m bins, color by p95 delta(streaming vs blocking) computed client-side
Trace link: when p95 > baseline+2σ, sample 20 recent traces with kv_cache_hit=false and >500 token-generation-ms
tasks: Ava: implement console panels + swimlane UI prototypes (in PR #4881)
Jordan (infra): add histogram buckets and low-cardinality 'io.mode' tag in metrics pipeline (PR #10234)
Maya (runtime): emit streamChunkLatency spans & attach chunk_index, request_shape (PR #2158)
Ravi: author runbook and alert rules, coordinate on SLO thresholds with SRE
QA: create synthetic workloads to validate streaming vs blocking percentile deltas
acceptance_criteria: Snapshotboard shows p50/p95/p99 for top 50 routes across models with streaming/blocking columns
Each percentile cell links to at least 5 correlated traces from last 30m (when available)
Alert fires in staging during synthetic regression test and maps to swimlane entries
Dashboard renders within 2s for default 1h window (client-side pagination & server filtering)
rollout_plan: Stage: deploy runtime hook and metrics pipeline changes to staging cluster, run synthetic tests
Canary: enable dashboard in limited orgs (redwood-internal, ops) for 48h
GA: enable for all orgs and add to default observability collection
Post-mortem: collect false-positive/false-negative alerts and refine thresholds over 2 weeks
risks_and_mitigations: High-cardinality explosion from adding tags -> mitigation: limit io.mode to two values and route/model tag to top-k only; fallback: rollup to 'route_group'
Trace volume increases -> mitigation: dynamic sampling on non-error/low-latency traces and targeted sampling when percentiles deviate
Alert noise on low-traffic routes -> mitigation: only enable delta alerts for routes above traffic threshold (>100 reqs/min)
